science.relativeGrowth: (1/N) dN/dt; r for J and r(1-N/K) for S
science.timeHorizon: Reach at least 99.5% of K, then continue another 1.5/r years; round the horizon up to a practical tick interval.
science.verticalScale: Both start with 0-500 individuals and 100 per division. S stays fixed. The J linear domain expands continuously with a smooth shoulder and at least 10% headroom, without discrete range jumps; all geometry derives deterministically from the current time.
assumptions: Constant positive r and K; no migration.
Illustrative continuous predictions, not measured data for a species.
The S curve approaches K smoothly and is never artificially clamped to K.
N0 above K/2 has no later inflection, so the K/2 jump is disabled. N0 equal to K/2 starts at peak growth speed.
Finite-period percentage growth is distinct from instantaneous relative growth r.
science.comparisonCurves: Each plot includes the other analytical growth model as a light-gray dashed curve, with identical N0, r and current time, mapped to that plot's linear axes. On the fixed S plot the J comparison ends exactly at the upper boundary with a continuation arrow, never clamped to K or compressed to fit.
